title: Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport has confirmed that Pedro Clerot will continue with the team for a second season in FIA Formula 3 in 2027.

Clerot had a strong rookie campaign with Rodin, finishing sixth in the Drivers' Championship helped by his five podiums – which include a Feature Race 1 victory at the final round in Madrid.

Prior to that, the 19-year-old won the 2022 Brazilian F4 title and finished fourth in the 2025 Formula Regional European Championship.

Clerot is now set to return for a second season in Formula 3, and the Brazilian driver expressed his delight at being able to do so in an environment where he feels very comfortable.

“I’m very happy to be staying with Rodin for my second year in FIA F3,” said Clerot. “We’ve built a really strong relationship this season and achieved some great results, improving race after race. I’ve felt at home with the team since day one, so continuing this journey together is very special.

“I believe we have what it takes to fight at the front next season, and I’m excited to see what we can achieve together.”

Rodin Motorsport Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “We’re delighted to continue our relationship with Pedro for another season in FIA Formula 3. He’s really impressed the team this year, showing strong pace and making great progress throughout the season. To see him take his maiden win in Madrid was a fantastic way to end the year and a result that reflects the progress he’s made. We’re looking forward to building on that next season and seeing what we can achieve together.”

title: TRIDENT confirm the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have announced the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 campaign – the first confirmed driver for the upcoming season.

Having made the step up from karting in 2023, Nakamura-Berta boasts an impressive record in single seaters having won 2025 Italian F4 and E4 Championships titles.

In 2026, the Williams Driver Academy member won Formula Regional Middle East Trophy title, and he also finished third in the Formula Regional European Championship.

Nakamura-Berta is now set to graduate to Formula 3 in 2027, and at the announcement, he expressed his delight at the opportunity to race with TRIDENT.

“I’m pleased to be stepping up to F3 with TRIDENT Motorsport while still having the ongoing support of the Williams F1 Team Driver Academy,” said Nakamura-Berta.

“Finishing the season strongly in FREC and having the opportunity to join such a competitive team in F3 gives me great confidence as I look ahead to my F3 debut next year. A big thank you to everyone involved who helped get me here.”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are extremely pleased to announce the arrival of Kean Nakamura-Berta at TRIDENT Motorsport for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship season. Kean is a driver we have known and followed for some time, and he has demonstrated he has all the qualities needed to take this important step. His journey, from karting to Formula Regional, has been marked by constant growth and impressive results. It will be a pleasure to begin this collaboration and work together to best prepare for such an important campaign. We are convinced that Trident represents the ideal environment to allow Kean to continue his growth and express his full potential in the FIA Formula 3 series.”

Williams F1 Team Sporting Director Sven Smeets also added: “It's a proud moment to see Kean step up to F3 with Trident Motorsport for his rookie season. He has made impressive progress since joining the Academy this year, and this opportunity is a culmination of the hard work and dedication he's shown across a long and hard-fought title campaign, backed by an already outstanding record. This is a great moment for the Driver Academy, and a fitting reflection of the opportunities it creates for the next generation of talented drivers.”

title: Clerot reflects on ‘really special’ Madrid weekend after claiming maiden victory
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot was pleased to bring a very “successful season” to a close with a special performance in Madrid – the Brazilian claiming his maiden Formula 3 victory in Feature Race 1.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was impressive at the Madring circuit, missing out on pole position by 0.012s in Qualifying 1 on Friday.

Clerot was then in the fight for pole on his final lap in Qualifying 2 but hit the barrier at the last corner and settled for third place.

The Brazilian driver then made a great start from P2 in Feature Race 1 to take the lead and the victory before adding another podium to his weekend tally with a P3 in Sunday’s race.

Speaking on his way out of the paddock with his two trophies in hand, Clerot reflected on a strong few days in the Spanish capital.

Clerot achieved his maiden win in Formula 3 in dominant style in Feature Race 1

“It was a really special, really special weekend,” he said. “It is really good to finally show what we had, maybe I'd say the whole year in terms of pace.

“Obviously, I'm not going to say luck was on our side, we did the work, we put a lot there in qualifying and we had a very good start yesterday.

“We controlled the race, had really good pace, and the car was incredible. The team did an amazing job, obviously driving was on point as well this weekend, so I’m really happy to put a very strong weekend to end the year.”

Speaking more about Feature Race 2, Clerot spoke about his mindset when out on track, admitted a move on Ugo Ugochukwu was never really on, but not for a lack of effort on his part.

“It's very difficult to overtake around here,” he said. “Obviously I was thinking more about the points as well. We're fighting for the team's championship as well, so just took it a little bit more careful today.

Clerot made sure to keep it clean out on track to achieve the best results

“But I didn't really have the opportunity to try to go for the overtake with Ugo. I know he was risking a bit more than me by fighting the championship.

“But anyway it’s another podium, another 15 points in the bag, we showed really good pace on such a difficult track like this, and to be this competitive is very nice, so I'm very happy.”

title: Taponen reflects on ‘satisfying’ end to the season after victory in Madrid
excerpt:
Tuukka Taponen claimed his maiden FIA Formula 3 victory in the Madrid Feature Race 2 – and that earned him third place in the Drivers’ Championship.

The MP Motorsport driver had a great final round, finishing third in Qualifying 1 and taking pole position in Qualifying 2.

Taponen would convert that into a podium in Feature Race 1 and held off champion Ugo Ugochukwu in Feature Race 2 to take the victory.

Speaking at the end of the weekend, the Finnish driver says staying ahead of his Campos Racing rival was vital to the victory.

title: ‘We’ve been incredible all season’ says Slater as he reflects on 2026 campaign and title loss
excerpt:
Freddie Slater admitted he was gutted to have not fought for the title in the way he wanted in Madrid. But he also paid tribute to rival Ugo Ugochukwu, Campos Racing and his team TRIDENT.

The British driver went into the weekend with a 15-point lead over Ugochukwu in the Standings, but was 17th in Qualifying 1 and eighth in Qualifying 2 after dealing with an issue on his car.

Ugochukwu, on the other hand, was fourth and second, and on a track where it is tough to overtake, Slater could not do much to catch up with his rival in all three races.

Both drivers were tied going into Sunday’s final Feature Race, and with Ugochukwu second and Slater seventh, the American took the title.

Reflecting on it all afterwards, Slater said: “Obviously a little bit gutted with the end result, but fundamentally we had too many things go wrong. The Feature Race in Monza, that was the start of it, and then this weekend in qualifying we had too many issues.

“On a track like this it's very difficult to overtake as well, so when you're at the back or in the mid-pack it's always going to be difficult. To be fair, fair play to Ugo and Campos, they had a good weekend.

Slater struggled in Qualfying in Madrid as he and TRIDENT struggled with an issue

“But we didn't really get the fight we wanted with the issues we had but overall it doesn't detract from the season we've had.

“We've done an amazing job all year to be a rookie with the performances we've had, we’ve been incredible all year. So it's just a shame that sometimes motorsport is like that, but that's how it is sometimes.”

Reflecting on the season as a whole, Slater had one win, three pole positions and eight podiums in total. Despite it not leading to the title, he views the year with a huge amount of positivity.

“I think as a rookie, trying to gain the experience and get on level with the second-year drivers as quick as I could has been really well managed,” he said.

“The pace has been incredible all year, very consistent, and executed all the time. Unfortunately there's some variables that went the wrong way out of our control, and those affect the results.

“They came at the worst possible time if I'm honest, because obviously there's no time now to catch up, it's over. So a little bit gutted the way we couldn't really finish the job off and really fight for it and show what we have been all season.

Slater's 2027 plans are already set as he will race in Formula 2 with Invicta Racing

“But it doesn't take away what we've done all year. We've done an amazing job, and I couldn't have done that without my team, TRIDENT. So a massive thank you to them.”

Slater’s 2027 plans have already been announced as he will step up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing. His goal now is to make sure he is ready for the challenges that lie ahead.

“We’ve still been fighting for another championship,” he continued. "It's another year done and another championship nearly won. So it's been an impressive career so far.

“But now there's some exciting things hopefully to come in the future. Still a steep hill to climb, that's for sure. So I need to continue to keep pushing and try and develop into a better driver, that's the aim of the game.

“So we're going to have a nice off-season, mostly with friends and family, and relax a little bit. But also get ready for next year to see what that holds.”

title: TITLE-WINNING ANALYSIS: The moment that earned Ugochukwu the 2026 title
excerpt:
In case you had not heard, Ugo Ugochukwu is the 2026 Drivers' Champion.

The Campos Racing driver outduelled rival Freddie Slater to the title in Madrid, overturning a 15-point deficit across the weekend. So, how did he do it?

We could look at the whole season – the dominant victories, the seven podiums and the eye-catching overtakes – but one moment in Monza sticks out as being far more important than the rest.

FIGHTBACK IN MONZA

Ugochukwu led the Standings for the first six rounds but lost his lead to Slater at the final race weekend before the summer break in Budapest.

The 19-year-old came to Monza second in the Standings and trailing his rival by eight points. But a messy Friday left him towards the back of the field, while Slater took pole position.

Ugochukwu's come back started after he was spun around at the start of the Monza Feature Race

Ugochukwu made his way up to P13 in the Sprint, showing the pace he had, but on Sunday, with his rival leading, the Campos driver was tagged into a spin by his teammate Théophile Nael.

This dropped the American down to last, but then his fightback started. As while Slater was starting to struggle with an issue and fall through the field, Ugochukwu was moving up.

The TRIDENT driver eventually stopped on track while Ugochukwu took the chequered flag in P8.

At one stage, Ugochukwu was looking at a deficit of more than 40 points going to Madrid, but he left Italy just 15 points behind.

In the paddock afterwards, the mood within the Campos camp was upbeat because they knew this was best case scenario, and they rode that positive momentum home to Madrid.

Ugochukwu came to Madrid with a 15 point deficit to Slater in the title fight

A HUGE FRIDAY IN MADRID

Campos and Ugochukwu were quick in the Madrid in-season test last month – setting the fastest time and leading two of the four sessions.

But Slater and TRIDENT topped the other two sessions, so they were also confident, and Free Practice form showed that both drivers would be competitive.

However there was a twist in Qualifying. Slater had an issue, while Ugochukwu was in the fight for pole The British driver had to pit early in Qualifying 1, and ended up in P17, while Ugochukwu was fourth.

Slater, running with the issue still managed to finish eighth in Qualifying 2, but it was not enough, with Ugochukwu in second and narrowly missing out on pole by 0.022s.

KEEPING IT CLEAN IN THE RACES

Going into the races Ugochukwu had the upper hand. Slater had to fight his way through the field from P17 for the Sprint Race and the first Feature.

Ugochukwu kept things controlled in all the races in Madrid

The American took P8 in the reverse grid Sprint, while his rival was down in P18. Slater then crashed out in Feature Race 1 as Ugochukwu finished in fourth.

The pendulum was swinging towards Ugochukwu, and Slater’s crash underlined it. At that same moment he hit the wall, the Campos driver was running wheel-to-wheel with Jin Nakamura and narrowly avoided the barrier at Turn 5.

It showed the fine margins in this title fight and it meant that Ugochukwu and Slater were now tied on points going into Feature Race 2.

19 LAPS OF QUIET DRAMA

Waking up on Sunday, Ugochukwu knew a clean race would make him champion.

Starting in second, a clean getaway and first few corners would give him one hand on the trophy, and that is what he got.

The only thing Ugochukwu might have wanted was to have taken the lead from Taponen at Turn 1. But the Finnish driver did well to cut him off at the start.

The Campos driver won the championship by 14 points after a strong performance in Madrid

From there, it was a case of ticking off the laps, making no mistakes, and that meant Slater had to do all the work to catch him.

Ugochukwu kept within the DRS of Taponen for much of the race and made sure he was never at risk of having to defend from Clerot, before crossing the line in second.

With Slater in seventh, the Campos driver had done enough to win the title by 14 points.

Winning a championship is a season long affair, as from the opening round in Melbourne to the final weekend in Madrid, Ugochukwu scored more points than every other driver.

But in a championship so close and with the margins so tight, there are moments that stick out as being incredibly pivotal.

For Ugochukwu, it might not have been his best result of the season, but that P8 in the Monza Feature Race was vital. That comeback drive could be why he left Madrid as the 2026 FIA Formula 3 champion.

title: ‘This was my main goal’ says Ugochukwu after sealing Formula 3 title in Madrid
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu is the 2026 Drivers’ Champion, completing what he believes has been the best season of his career to date.

The Campos Racing driver went into Sunday’s Feature Race 2 tied on points with Freddie Slater, and by finishing second, compared to his rival in eighth, he claimed the title.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, a delighted Ugochukwu spoke of the importance of winning this championship.

“I'm feeling really good, for sure,” said Ugochukwu. “This was the main goal at the start of the year, to get the championship.

“I think after quali we knew we did our job, we did the main task, and today, and yesterday, it was just about execution and getting the points and bringing it home.

“There was a little bit of pressure which is pretty normal. This last weekend was definitely the most important one of the championship, with two Features.

Ugochukwu kept things calm and controlled out on track on his way to the title in Madrid

“So, quali was pressure to get the job done. I thought I performed with the pressure, I had the right risk versus reward and didn't make any mistakes. Ultimately today, we benefited off the good quali.

“Today I knew what I had to do to win the championship. So, it was in my hands to keep it clean, keep the cars behind at bay, and just bring it home to the line.”

This result represented a massive turnaround for Ugochukwu as he went into Sunday’s Feature Race in Monza starting at the back of the field, while Slater went from pole.

But with his rival not finishing and him making a comeback to the points, he set himself up for a title showdown in Madrid.

Speaking about his mentality through it all, Ugochukwu said: “I think coming into this weekend, we were quite fortunate to be able to come in 15 points behind.

Ugochukwu is Campos Racing's first FIA Formula 3 Drivers' Champion

“We used that to our advantage. 15 points is still a decent gap, but I knew that was enough to put a bit of pressure on our rivals, and ultimately, we managed to perfect this last weekend, execute it well, and that's what gave us the championship.”

Reflecting more on his season long battle with Slater, Ugochukwu says it was one he enjoyed.

“It was a great battle throughout the year and we really enjoyed it,” he said. “I think beginning of the year, we knew from testing and Round 1 that it might be us two at the end that we would be battling for the championship.

“But to come down like that, to the wire, with equal points in the last race was pretty crazy. So just obviously really happy to get it done and to clinch the title and to come out on top.”

Looking back on the year, Ugochukwu started 2026 winning the Formula Regional Oceania Championship in New Zealand ahead of Slater.

Ugochukwu achieved the goal he set out to at the beginning of the season

The 19-year-old ranks this season as the best of his career to date.

“I think this year is probably one of my top ones of my racing journey, my racing career, 2026 as a whole,” added Ugochukwu.

“Really happy that I've been able to show what I can do. Two titles this year this being my second, and for sure this is the one I really, really wanted to get done.

For sure this is a great step for my career, really important, and it's a good step for what's to come.”

title: Thoughts of a Champion - Ugo Ugochukwu
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome, everyone, to the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champions Press Conference. Many congratulations to our FIA Formula 3 Champion, driving for Campos Racing, Ugo Ugochukwu. Ugo, congratulations. You were locked in a tight battle with Freddie Slater all season. What was your mindset coming here to Madrid with such a close championship battle?

Ugo Ugochukwu: For sure, I was not expecting to come into the final race equal on points, but it made it very exciting. I think we did a good job all weekend. We put ourselves in a good position after qualifying and in the races, so today was just about executing and doing our job properly. P2 was not a bad result. I was just trying to manage my tyres. We knew that was what I needed to win the championship, so it was just about getting it home.

FIA Formula 3: Two victories and seven podiums. You have had a lot of great moments, but is there one moment in the season that stands out for you?

Ugochukwu: I think there are a few. For sure, round one in Melbourne was super special. That was my first win in Formula 3 and it gave me a lot of confidence to continue pushing throughout the season, knowing that we were in the championship fight. Monza was also important, coming back to score a few points. We were fortunate to come into this weekend only 15 points behind, and that really allowed us to apply pressure, attack and ultimately take the championship.

FIA Formula 3: You came back for a second season after a tough rookie year. How much have you learned and matured since stepping into the Formula 3 paddock, and how proud are you of the level of performance you have shown this year?

Ugochukwu: I am super happy. Overall, I think I have improved and evolved as a driver. That is also my goal for the following years, to keep performing better and better. This title is a testament to that, so I am really happy with the work we have put in with the team. I am super happy for them as well, clinching the Teams’ Championship yesterday, and today we got the job done to seal both. It has been pretty much a perfect season for us.

FIA Formula 3: You led the Drivers’ Championship for much of the season, but was there any point when you doubted your title hopes?

Ugochukwu: I would not say I doubted, but there were definitely some points when it looked like we had lost the advantage and needed to come back a little bit. I always kept the faith that I would be able to do it. I had a lot of confidence coming into this weekend, despite being 15 points behind, and I knew it was still possible. We executed everything well, and that allowed us to get the job done.

FIA Formula 3: You are Campos Racing’s first FIA Formula 3 Champion. What does that mean to you, and how key have they been to your success this season?

Ugochukwu: It is super special. The whole team is very happy with this. Our goal at the beginning of the year was to fight for the championship, and that is what we have done. We managed to come out on top, so I cannot thank each and every one of them enough for all their hard work. We have worked well together since before the season started, and I think that really paid off. Starting the championship well is always important, and we finished the season well this weekend too. I am really happy to clinch this first title for Campos.

FIA Formula 3: What is next for the FIA Formula 3 Champion?

Ugochukwu: We will see. Formula 2 is, of course, the next logical step up the ladder towards everyone’s dream of Formula 1. For now, I am just enjoying this title and this championship. The whole of 2026 has been very good for me, winning two championships, and we will see what 2027 brings.

title: Round 9 Post-Feature Race 2 Thoughts from the Top Three
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Tuukka Taponen, from pole position to first at the flag, your first win of the 2026 season. It was the last race of the season, but that must still be a great moment for you?

Tuukka Taponen: Yes, these last three weekends have been super good for us. We were really struggling earlier this season and it was not looking so good, to be honest. But we have done such a good job and worked so much to improve our performance. I think the results speak for themselves. It has been a super end to the year.

FIA Formula 3: Can we talk about the race today? You started from pole position alongside the not-yet FIA Formula 3 champion, Ugo Ugochukwu. In yesterday's races, every time, P2 became P1 at the first corner. Did you have that in mind when the lights went out?

Taponen: It was on my mind already last night when I was going to sleep. It was really stressful because I knew it needed to be a clean, good start. There was no need to do anything special, just make a decent start and it would be enough. That is what we did and we managed to stay ahead.

FIA Formula 3: Towards the final laps, Ugo came closer and was putting pressure on you. Was it a different kind of pressure knowing that he had everything at stake? Were you a little more relaxed seeing him behind you?

Taponen: I knew Ugo's situation. I was pretty sure he was not going to attack me. I was managing at the front and controlling the gap behind. Then I was going to push a little more at the end to get the fastest lap, which I did on the final lap. I was just keeping it on track and driving smoothly.

FIA Formula 3: At the end of the day, this is P3 in the 2026 standings for you. Knowing how difficult your season has been, are you happy with that finishing position?

Taponen: Yes, after everything we have had, I am super happy. I could not believe this a few weekends ago. I was far from P3, but it has been super close in this championship from P3 to around P10. I knew everything was possible here, especially with two Feature Races. Qualifying was key because overtaking is very difficult. I am super happy with how the season finished.

FIA Formula 3: Are your 2027 plans already set, or were you waiting for that final result before thinking about them?

Taponen: For me, it is a difficult situation. I do not have a place for next year. Struggling with the financial side is part of motorsport, but we are trying our best to do something next year. I hope we can make a decision soon.

FIA Formula 3: Thank you very much, Tuukka. An excellent job this weekend and best of luck for the future. Ugo Ugochukwu, you came into this morning at Madrid in P2, with your title rival having scored zero points yesterday and starting P8 behind you. Did you feel relaxed coming into the race, or are you never relaxed when you know you are racing for the championship?

Ugo Ugochukwu: It is hard. In a way, I knew I was in a good position to get the championship today and I knew what I needed to do to win the title, but I was not fully relaxed. You think about all the little things that can happen and that you need to stay on top of. Today was executed quite well. I knew I had a good chance on the inside to maybe go for the lead at the start, but Tuukka did a good job defending his position. From there, it felt like a very long race. I just had to manage the tyre and the gap to the drivers behind me. That is what we did. To win the championship is testament to the consistency and the job we have done throughout the year.

FIA Formula 3: Yesterday we saw three races, two Formula 3 races and one Formula 2 race, and every time P2 was leading into Turn 1. Were you playing it safer than anything else, simply wanting a clean start?

Ugochukwu: For sure, a clean start was on our minds. We could not afford a stall, a jump start or anything like that. Getting into the lead at the start would still have been nice because controlling from the front is always a little easier and cleaner, but I knew I just had to adapt to whatever situation I was in. Whether that was P2 or P3, I just managed the race as best as I could. I tried to make a move later on and put on a bit of pressure, but Tuukka was quick in the right places and I could not get quite close enough. Qualifying was the key to this weekend and we executed that well to put ourselves in a good position today on such a tricky track.

FIA Formula 3: With all the pressure and what was potentially waiting at the end, was that the most difficult race of the season for you?

Ugochukwu: It definitely was one of the most difficult races. In terms of performance, we were quick and I did not have too much pressure from behind, but at the same time you cannot afford any mistakes with such a big thing on the line. I made sure to keep it clean. We have seen a lot of damage to the cars from the kerbs here throughout the weekend and in testing as well, so I tried to be gentle with the car and make sure it reached the line.

FIA Formula 3: There was one final Safety Car period at the end and one final lap of racing. During that Safety Car period, did you think it was done, or did you wait until the chequered flag before you could really let it all go?

Ugochukwu: Initially, I thought it was going to end under the Safety Car because I saw there was no work being done on the car. My engineer also thought it was going to be over, but then he came on the radio and said there would be one more lap. I started working on my tyres again to be fully prepared for that lap. I held my breath for one lap, and once I crossed the line I could relax a little.

FIA Formula 3: From all of us at FIA Formula 3, huge congratulations on a great 2026 season. We look forward to seeing what you do next. Pedro Clerot, P3 in today's final Feature Race of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship. It is another podium after your win yesterday in the first Feature Race. What an amazing weekend you have had. How are you feeling right now?

Pedro Clerot: Very good. It was obviously a very strong weekend on our side, both for me and the team. I am very happy that we could end the season on a high. As I said before, it was a very tough year for us, but to finish like this makes it extra special. I am very happy with the work we put in after the test and also Monza. We knew coming here that we had a good chance to fight, but I try not to think about results and just focus on the work. That is what we did and that is what we achieved. Yesterday was a very good race, winning and controlling it completely. Today, we brought home good points for both the Teams' and Drivers' Championships. I am obviously very happy. Maybe we could have fought for a little more, but I will take it. After such a hard year, it is good to finish like this.

FIA Formula 3: This was your rookie season in Formula 3. What did you learn from your first season in this championship? We know it is one of the most competitive championships out there.

Clerot: For sure. You do not get much driving in this series. It is all about adapting and being in control of the things you can control. I am very happy with what we achieved. Five podiums this season is something I never imagined doing in my rookie season. We always aim to fight for the championship. It was not to be this time, but I am very happy with the work we did with Rodin this year. I have learned a lot. Rodin have been like a family to me this year and welcomed me very well from day one, so I am very happy with what we achieved. Hopefully, I can get some more silverware in whatever comes next.

FIA Formula 3: The end of the season always brings questions about what is next. You will not reveal your plans, but do you already know them, and are you happy with them?

Clerot: Yes, I am very happy with how the plans look for next year. Obviously, I cannot share them, but it is going to be very nice. I am very happy to be going where I am going. I think it is going to be a very strong year. We have the capability to fight for championships in whatever comes next. I am looking forward to it, but I also want to enjoy some free time now, spend time with my family, go back home to Brazil and celebrate a little.

FIA Formula 3: Good job on your first season, Pedro, and best of luck for what comes next.

title: FEATURE RACE 2: Taponen wins as Ugochukwu seals 2026 Drivers' title
excerpt:
Tuukka Taponen was victorious in Madrid for MP Motorsport, winning the second Feature Race of the weekend as Ugo Ugochukwu secured the 2026 Drivers' Championship in P2 to become the first F3 Champion from the United States.

The Finn led every lap en route to the top step of the podium, with Ugochukwu remaining close and adding another podium to his record to seal the title. Rodin Motorsport's Pedro Clerot rounded out the podium in third position.

AS IT HAPPENED

Taponen covered off Ugochukwu immediately at Turn 1 and he retained the lead over the Campos Racing driver. Freddie Slater dropped a place to Yevan David on the run to Turn 5 to make his road to the title tougher.

With DRS enabled on Lap 3, David looked to make a move on Enzo Deligny at Turn 5 but couldn't get through, offering a brief chance for Slater to look at the AIX Racing driver into Turn 7, ultimately falling back into line in ninth.

Slater was on the attack on Lap 5, and he rounded the Sri Lankan into Turn 2 to take eighth.

Up ahead, Ugochuwku was content to sit within a second of the race leader and keep Clerot behind in third.

Lap 10 and Slater was onto the back of Deligny and tried an audacious look into Turn 7, but the Van Amersfoort Racing driver was able to remain ahead.

Taponen held the lead at the start and led every lap to earn his first win in F3

With the laps ticking by, Slater was looking to get creative and shaped for a move into Turn 13, but once again found the door shut.

Taito Kato was looking to round out his season with another podium, and was close to Clerot in the battle for third. A big lock-up into Turn 17 almost left the Japanese driver sailing into the back of the Rodin, but he managed to avoid a collision and continued in fourth.

David was relegated to 10th after a big slide at Turn 18 allowed Ernesto Rivera to capitalise and take ninth in the Campos on Lap 16.

Hiyu Yamakoshi came to a halt with three laps remaining, bringing out the Safety Car. The marshals were able to recover the Van Amersfoort Racing car in time to leave us with a one-lap shootout for the victory and the '26 title.

Taponen got a good restart and led the pack onto the final lap with a comfortable lead over Ugochuwku, who had Clerot for close company.

Despite the late drama, Taponen had control of the race and secured his maiden win in FIA Formula 3 in the final race of the year.

The Finn's victory lifted him and the team to third in the Drivers' and Teams' Championships to finish the 2026 season

Ugochukwu crossed the line in P2 to claim the Drivers' Championship and complete his comeback in the title race, while Clerot completed the podium in third.

Kato was fourth ahead of Mattia Colnaghi, Alessandro Giusti, Deligny and Slater, who finished eighth. Rivera and David rounded out the final top 10 of the season.

KEY QUOTE – Ugo Ugochukwu, Campos Racing

“We did it, FIA F3 Champions! Super, super happy and I can't thank the team enough for an amazing year. Today was not a bad race with P2. We knew we just had to keep it clean to clinch the title, and that's what we did. No mistakes, brought it home and super pleased."

THE CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Ugo Ugochukwu is the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Drivers' Champion, finishing on 159 points. Freddie Slater winds up second in the Standings on 145 points. Tuukka Taponen's win lifts the Finn up to third in the Championship ahead of Taito Kato in fourth, 109 points to 105. Théophile Nael finishes fifth on countback ahead of Pedro Clerot on 88 points each, and the top five drivers that graduate up to FIA Formula 2 in 2027 will receive prize money ahead of the next step in their careers.

Campos Racing are 2026 Teams' Champions already, with the team's final total standing at 334 points. TRIDENT finish second on 217, while MP Motorsport jump up to third and 208 points, ahead of ART Grand Prix in fourth on 189. Van Amersfoort Racing complete the top five with 168 points.

UP NEXT

We have reached the end of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 campaign. Keep up to date with the latest news, interviews and events via the official website and social media channels.

title: Adrian Campos: 'It's amazing to win back-to-back titles but we must continue to improve'
excerpt:
Campos Racing successfully retained the FIA Formula 3 Teams' Championship title, securing the title on home soil in Madrid.

The Spanish outfit had all three drivers in the points on Saturday in Feature Race 1, and eponymous Team Principal Adrian Campos was pleased to add a second F3 title to their history.

However, the Campos team boss was eager to underline the job was not done yet, with expectations to fight for the remaining titles across F3 and FIA Formula 2 this season.

"Right now, I am 25% satisfied. There are still three more that we need to do our best to achieve. Tomorrow, there is another race, Ugo needs to do the job and try to win the Drivers' Championship.

"It's amazing winning back-to-back here in FIA F3, but something that we lost last year was the Drivers' Championship, and this is something that obviously is a goal this year also, so we can keep improving every year.

"Every year, our goal is to improve what we did in the previous one and it's happening so far. Regarding F3, if we win both championships, then our goal will be defending it, and we will do our best to do it. But we can always do better.

"Everyone will be improving, everyone will learn, we'll get better, we'll get quicker and we will need to in order to stay here, and we will do our best so we can do that."

Ugochukwu will have a chance to make it a Campos double in F3 this season on Sunday

Leading the team's charge in Feature Race 1, Ugo Ugochukwu finished up fourth and drew level on points in the Drivers' Championship, leading the way on countback courtesy of two race victories to Freddie Slater's one.

Campos praised his driver's performances across 2026, highlighting that all three have impressed, with Théophile Nael and Ernesto Rivera still in contention to finish inside the top five in the Standings.

"All of them have been outstanding, especially Ugo, because he's the one that is now leading and has the chance to win the Drivers' title tomorrow," Campos continued.

"But the other two have been always there. We arrived here P2, P3 and P4 in the championship, so having three drivers in the top four is something that we need to be proud of, so I'm very happy with that.

"Ernesto especially, because he missed the first round because of an injury and when he was back in the car, he was really strong, brought a lot of points and wins to the team."

Looking ahead to Sunday's curtain-closing Feature Race, Campos underlined that nothing was settled yet in terms of the Drivers' Championship battle.

While Ugochukwu goes from second on the grid and Slater is in eighth, Saturday's Feature Race showed that nothing is certain.

The Campos Team Principal added that the team would endeavor to maximise their chances by staying ahead of the TRIDENT driver, rather than go all out for glory.

"This is a circuit that is not easy to overtake around, so after the quali that we had, the bad luck that Freddie had in Qualifying, everything has gone a bit more in our favour.

"But, we need to keep doing what we have been doing, stay out of trouble, make no mistakes, no crashes and finish the race in the points and in front of Freddie. That's our goal tomorrow."

title: Round 9 Post Feature Race 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following Feature Race 1 in Madrid. Joining us are P3 from MP Motorsport, Tuukka Taponen, P2 from ART Grand Prix, Taito Kato, and race winner Pedro Clerot from Rodin Motorsport. Pedro, congratulations. Your first FIA Formula 3 victory. How does that feel?

Pedro Clerot: Unbelievable. I have no words to describe what I am feeling right now. We knew it was going to be all about the start and together with the team we came up with a very good plan. We made the changes we needed from the race this morning and maximised everything within our control. It was a bit of a messy race and I am glad everyone is okay after the crash. We managed things well and then pushed flat out to the end. I am really happy to take the win and I think we deserve it.

FIA Formula 3: Can you take us through the opening lap?

Clerot: The start was really good. We knew it would be all about the launch and I felt very confident already on the Formation Lap. I told my engineer we should keep everything the same. When the lights went out I got a great launch with no wheelspin. I was already side-by-side with Taito into Turn 1 and from there it was about making the corner. After the Red Flag and two Safety Car restarts it was a little trickier, but the car was absolutely flying. The team gave me an amazing car and I enjoyed every moment out there.

FIA Formula 3: Tell us about the celebration at the finish.

Clerot: It was the phone celebration. It has not been exactly the year we wanted, but I knew this moment would come sooner or later. There has been a lot of noise around not performing and today we proved people wrong. We showed we are here to fight and achieve great things.

FIA Formula 3: You start P3 tomorrow. What do you think is possible?

Clerot: Let's see. Tuukka had a fairly relaxed race today. I am aiming to score good points and capitalise on any opportunities that come. The car was very quick today and I think we can improve even more for tomorrow, but for now I want to enjoy this moment.

__FIA Formula 3: Taito, congratulations. Your fourth podium of the season. How does P2 feel? __

Taito Kato: It is a mixed feeling because I started from pole position and wanted to win. Huge congratulations to Pedro. His pace was very strong. From my side the car was really good, but it was difficult to overtake. Still, P2 is a strong result and a good haul of points. The car was great to drive and I think it puts us in a good position for tomorrow as well.

FIA Formula 3: Can you talk us through your opening lap?

Kato: We had a small issue with the car before the Formation Lap and the team did a great job fixing it. I was a little worried because things were not going smoothly and that created some frustration. Even so, I managed to stay focused and convert it into a P2 finish, which makes me happy.

FIA Formula 3: Tuukka, congratulations on your second podium of the season. How does that one feel?

Tuukka Taponen: It was a good race and it went exactly as I wanted. I made a clean start, stayed in P3, watched what was happening up front, then started to manage the race and look after the tyres. At the end I was able to go for the fastest lap and achieve it, so from my side it was a very good race.

FIA Formula 3: Ugo was chasing you towards the finish. How were you able to keep him behind?

Taponen: I think Ugo was trying a similar strategy, creating a gap to the cars ahead and then pushing at the end. I managed to be quicker than him and I think he also had to think about the championship. He needed solid points, whereas I could focus on my own race.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P3.

title: FEATURE RACE 1: Clerot earns maiden win in Madrid as Campos Racing seal Teams’ title
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot impressively earned his first ever victory in Formula 3 with a dominant performance in the Madrid Feature Race 1.

After starting in P2, the Rodin Motorsport driver took the lead off the line and led every lap to take the win ahead of Taito Kato for ART Grand Prix and MP Motorsport’s Tuukka Taponen.

With Ugo Ugochukwu in fourth, Ernesto Rivera and Théophile Nael in eighth and ninth, Campos Racing sealed the 2026 Teams’ title – while the former went level with Freddie Slater in the Drivers’ Championship.

AS IT HAPPENED

It was a great start for Clerot from P2, taking the lead from Kato on the run to Turn 1. Behind them, Taponen held off Ugochukwu to keep third.

But a Red Flag was soon waved following a multi-car collision that started between Van Amersfoort Racing teammates Bruno Del Pino and Enzo Deligny at the entry of Turn 8.

This caused several other drivers to hit each other with Maciej Gladysz going into the rear of Fionn McLaughlin, while Fernando Barrichello, Woohyun Shin and José Garfias were also caught up in the incident.

TRIDENT’s title hopeful Slater also had slight contact with Hiyu Yamakoshi at Turn 1. The team used the stoppage to change his and his teammate Noah Stromsted’s front wing.

After the pause, Clerot led the field away in a rolling start on Lap 3. Ugochukwu started by putting pressure on Taponen for third place.

The race leader was showing great pace and with the fastest lap, put 1.4s between himself and Kato at the start of Lap 5.

Taponen was struggling and was over two seconds away from P2, with Ugochukwu right on the rear on the MP driver.

While his title rival was fighting up ahead, Slater locked up into Turn 1 while battling with Yamakoshi for P14. This put Kanato Le on alert, but the British driver held on.

Lap 8 saw a battle for P6 begin with Alessandro Giusti having a look at Rivera at the Turn 5 chicane, but the Campos driver held on.

Taponen looked to have steadied the ship with Ugochukwu two seconds behind and coming under pressure from Jin Nakamura.

There was a huge twist in the title fight on Lap 10 as Slater spun and hit the barrier at Turn 19, putting him out of the race and onto the sidelines.

Up ahead, Ugochukwu and Nakamura went wheel-to-wheel into Turn 5. The Campos driver narrowly escaped a hit the wall, while the Japanese driver gave the position back after going off track.

The Safety Car was called upon and once Slater’s car was cleared, racing resumed on Lap 12, with Clerot and Kato moving away from Taponen once again.

The ART driver was within DRS range on the next lap, while Ugochukwu was once again coming under pressure from Nakamura for P4.

Clerot had done well to extend his lead to 1.2s on Lap 17, while Taponen, having set the fastest time of the race, was starting to drop back and into the clutches of Ugochukwu.

In the battle for third in the championship, Rivera and Théophile Nael went wheel-to-wheel into Turn 5 on the final lap, with both drivers going off the track.

But at the front, Clerot was untroubled and crossed the line to earn his maiden victory in Formula 3. Kato took P2 ahead of Taponen, while Ugochukwu, by finishing fourth, ties Slater on points heading into Sunday’s Feature Race.

Nakamura finished fifth ahead of Giusti, Alex Powell and Rivera, with Nael ninth and Wharton taking the final point in P10.

This result also meant Campos Racing sealed the 2026 Teams’ Championship, their second consecutive title in Formula 3.

KEY QUOTE – Pedro Clerot, Rodin Motorsport

“I have no words to describe it. We knew it was all about the start, and we nailed it. Thanks to the team for the beautiful car. We were in control since Lap 1, bit of a messy one, glad everyone is okay, it was a big crash. Really happy, cannot thank the team enough. We needed this after Monza, so very happy.”

CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

In the Drivers’ Championship, Ugo Ugochukwu and Freddie Slater are tied on 141 points, although the former is on top having won more races. Taito Kato moves up to third on 91 points, ahead of Théophile Nael on 88 points and Ernesto Rivera on 85.

In the Teams’ Standings, Campos Racing sealed the title on 314 points, with TRIDENT second on 213. ART Grand Prix are up to third on 177, with Van Amersfoort Racing fourth on 162, and tied on points with MP Motorsport.

UP NEXT

The Drivers’ Championship will come down to Sunday’s Feature Race, the final piece of action in the 2026 season. Lights out is set for 09:55 local time.

There is plenty to play for in the fight for the championship podium and also funding for the top five drivers that will graduate to Formula 2 in 2027.

title: Round 9 Post-Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Hello and welcome to today's FIA Formula 3 Press Conference following the Sprint Race in Madrid. Joining us today in third place, Alex Powell for PREMA Racing. In second place, also for PREMA Racing, James Wharton. And in first place, winner of the Sprint Race, Théophile Naël for Campos Racing. First of all, starting with you Théophile, congratulations. That was your third win of the 2026 season and you looked to be in full control after taking P1. How happy are you with that race and your performance today?

Théophile Naël: Yeah, extremely happy to be the first winner in Madrid. Obviously, it has been a really good race for me and a really good start. Then it was about managing the tyres. There is no degradation on the tyres, but just some overheating on the front-left. I still managed to set my fastest lap in the final two laps, so I am extremely happy. It means that I managed the tyres quite well and I think it is a good indication for tonight's race.

FIA Formula 3: You mentioned the fact that you were flying and you set the fastest lap of the race several times. You looked to be enjoying your time out there in Madrid, and you are now the first-ever Formula 3 race winner at this track. How does that feel, and what are your general feelings about this layout?

Naël: I was a bit disappointed about my qualifying yesterday, but obviously to bounce back like that today is such an incredible feeling. It is a home race for the team as well. We are close to becoming Teams' Champions, so these are some good points for them and also for me, maybe to fight for third place this weekend. I am very happy. The pace was really good, so I am looking forward to both races tonight and tomorrow morning.

FIA Formula 3: Like you said, unfortunately the points gap means there are now only very slim hopes for the Formula 3 title, but a top-three finish is still possible. This is the end of your second season in Formula 3. You came into it to win it, but how does a top-three finish sound?

Naël: It is not where I wanted to be, to be honest, but I think still being in the top three could be something very positive for the future as well. The pace has been there throughout the whole season. There have been some disappointing race weekends from my side, but overall I am extremely happy. Three pole positions in a row at the beginning of the season was spot on. Then we had some issues in some races and some penalties that I could have avoided. But I would still be extremely happy if I can be in the top three at the end of the weekend.

FIA Formula 3: Your team, Campos Racing, could be crowned Teams' Champions this evening after the Feature Race. That must bring a lot of satisfaction as well.

Naël: Yeah, let's see. It can be done tonight, so hopefully we do our best. I will do the best I can to grab some points, whether it is one or two. It could be done tonight, so I would be extremely happy for them.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on a great race today and best of luck for the Feature Races coming up. James, moving on to you, congratulations as well. Your second podium of 2026. You will have been hoping for one place better today in the Sprint Race, but talk us through your race this morning.

James Wharton: To be honest, it is a bit bittersweet because we were starting from pole in the first race here in Madrid, and to get that win would have been quite special. But at the same time, if you had asked me at the start of the weekend whether I would take a podium in the Sprint Race, I would have taken it. I need to be happy with the work we are doing. At the end of the day, it has not been the season that we hoped for as a team or that I hoped for as a driver. It is hard seeing people you have competed against your whole life doing well and fighting for championships, so getting these podiums when they come is very important. Apart from the start, which was not amazing, although it was not super bad, it put me on the back foot. But when you finish second on a track like this with no mistakes after the start, I have to be happy with that. You have to take those positives during a tough season.

FIA Formula 3: Turn 5 might be the best overtaking spot around the circuit. You did not quite make it stick there, but how tough is that part of the track for completing a pass?

Wharton: To be honest, it probably would have been the first overtake in Madrid ever if I had done that. It did not quite pay off, and it is obviously not easy when you are the first person to arrive there on the first lap. At the same time, I feel the races will get more and more chaotic as the season comes to an end and people are really trying to do the best they can. Starting from P12 in the Feature Race this afternoon is the next chance to get some points, so I will be the one trying to make some moves.

FIA Formula 3: Formula 3 is the first championship to race in Madrid. Was that something you had in mind starting from pole position? We did not really know what to expect because this was the first race, so was that going through your mind?

Wharton: To be honest, I really wanted to get that first win around this track. It would have been something I could take away from 2026. I did not quite get the job done, but we felt tyre degradation was going to be a big issue. We thought there would be some, but it was not as clear as we expected, so maybe I could have pushed a little more at the start of the race. The lack of knowledge was quite tough. Normally, we go into a race really understanding what happened in previous years, but today we did not have that, so we were learning during the race itself. As you saw with Théophile, he kept getting faster. At the same time, we have to take the podium today. That is all we could have done.

FIA Formula 3: Will the Feature Race be easier with the data you collected, or perhaps more difficult because of the physical challenge of having to race again?

Wharton: It is obviously going to be a very different race. Starting P12 and starting P1 make for very different races. If you ask any driver, starting in that part of the grid is always more difficult. You have to be a little more careful with the people around you. But I feel there are opportunities to be had in this Feature Race at 6 p.m., when everyone has been awake since 6 a.m. Hopefully, everyone is a little more tired and some more mistakes happen, which is what we can capitalise on today.

FIA Formula 3: We will leave it there for now. Congratulations. Alex, thank you for waiting. Your first FIA Formula 3 podium, with P3 in the Sprint Race, in only your second round in the Championship. How satisfied are you with that result today?

Alex Powell: Of course, it is super cool to be on the podium. It was unexpected. Obviously, it was very last-minute to join for the final two rounds, but we have been pretty competitive since the start of the weekend, from Free Practice. We had pretty good potential and yesterday qualifying was executed pretty well. Today it was just about staying out of trouble and learning about tyre management, which is quite new for me as well. Then it was about staying clean and making it to the end of the race.

FIA Formula 3: Monza, the last race weekend, was your first round in Formula 3. We come here to Madrid, where the Formula 3 test took place a few weeks ago. Did this weekend feel a little easier because you knew the track and how the car would behave?

Powell: For sure. I think it is helpful for me, seeing as it is new for everyone. Monza was definitely a baptism of fire. It was a weekend of firsts, so it was about learning as much as possible. This weekend, I knew there was probably going to be a bit more opportunity. I am glad we capitalised on it in the Sprint Race, but of course we have two more races to look forward to and we will try to extract a little more.

FIA Formula 3: Looking at how the Sprint Race went this morning, what are your hopes for the Feature Race, and how do you think it will unfold for you starting from P11?

Powell: I think it is going to be an interesting one. Of course, we have the information from the Sprint Race, which can help us, but at the end of the day overtaking is quite tricky around here. It is just going to be about capitalising on other people's mistakes and looking forward, trying to make every opportunity count. We will see where we end up.

FIA Formula 3: Let's see. Thank you very much.

title: Taito Kato: 'We can win the Feature Races' after impressing in Madrid so far
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix's Taito Kato is thriving around the challenging Madring circuit, as the Japanese driver came from P12 on the Sprint Race grid to secure points.

Kato pulled off a brave overtake at Turn 5, rounding MP Motorsport's Tuukka Taponen for P10, before gaining another position once Enzo Delingy’s 10-second time penalty took effect.

Reflecting on his race, the Honda Formula Dream Project driver said he was happy with the overtake and added points to his 2026 tally.

"I think it was really great. Overall, really difficult to overtake here and I think you saw that in the race. There was no overtaking point, and really difficult to overtake the car in front, even with DRS.

"We had a good start and gained some points. I was able to overtake Pedro and then at that point, I was P11. Then, Lap 12 or 13 I was able to overtake Tuukka in front because he didn't have DRS.

"I had good top speed, I could go side-by-side into T5 and then brake later to move in front. But it was really tough to be honest. But happy to finally have gained the position."

Kato was one of the few overtakes in what was a tricky Sprint around the Madring. The ART driver said that the race was hugely important in terms of building data ahead of the first Feature Race on Saturday evening, and Sunday morning.

He added that he will need to work very hard with the team both during and after the race in order to extract the maximum performance in Sunday's event, as he targets a final round leap up to third in the Drivers' Championship.

"It's going to be the same situation in the two Feature Races I guess. I will just focus on the tyre saving and also managing the gap in front and behind.

"Good communication with the engineers. When you have to close or not because we need to get some data for the other Feature Race.

"So we need to get clean air. Because we start in P1 in the Feature Race, and P4 in the other Feature too. I think it's quite a different story as it was a Sprint Race. So we can gather as much data as we can.

"We had really good data from the Sprint Race. So I think we have really good car performance and good confidence for the two races.

"For sure we can get another win. We have a really good mindset from the Monza. Obviously, it was a mighty weekend in Monza. But still, I couldn't win the Feature Race. So I think this time the target is to win in the Feature."

title: SPRINT RACE: Nael in full control for third win of 2026
excerpt:
Théophile Nael earned the first ever race win around the Madring, taking the lead on the opening lap and controlling things from the front.

It was the Campos Racing driver's third win of the season, as PREMA Racing's James Wharton and Alex Powell completed the podium on a strong day for the Italian team.

AS IT HAPPENED

Wharton got a decent start from pole position, but it was Nael with the best launch, and he claimed the lead into Turn 1.

The Australian went wheel-to-wheel with the Frenchman into Turn 5 but went deep and had to skip across the chicane. The PREMA driver ceded the position later in the lap and was able to slot back into second ahead of teammate Powell.

The title contenders didn't make progress on the opening lap, with Ugo Ugochukwu retaining P9 while Freddie Slater dropped one position to 18th in the TRIDENT.

By Lap 5, Nael had extended his lead over the chasing PREMAs to over a second, putting him out of DRS range to the tune of 1.3s.

Alessandro Giusti had been running fourth but was told over team radio to cede the position to Bruno Del Pino. The Frenchman obliged out of Turn 17, dropping back to fifth and keeping Ernesto Rivera in his mirrors.

Having dropped out of DRS range to Del Pino, Giusti was coming under pressure from Rivera and the Mexican was told to attack by the Campos team over the radio on Lap 9.

Nael took the lead of the race into Turn 1 and never looked in trouble after the opening laps

Overtaking was proving tough, but Taito Kato showed it was possible, rounding Tuukka Taponen with DRS into Turn 5 to take the final points place in 10th.

Seventh on the road Enzo Deligny was then handed a 10-second time penalty on Lap 13 for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in an earlier defence of P7 from Jin Nakamura.

At the front though, nobody could catch Nael, who took fastest lap as well as race victory in a dominant display around the Madring.

PREMA Racing's Wharton and Powell rounded out the podium, the latter earning his maiden rostrum visit on his second weekend in F3.

Del Pino held off Giusti and Rivera for fourth. Deligny's penalty dropped him to 15th, promoting Nakamura, Ugochukwu, Kato and Taponen up once position each in the points.

Nael's win was his third of the 2026 campaign and lifted him to third in the Standings

KEY QUOTE - Théophile Nael, Campos Racing

"First victory of the weekend is for me. Super happy to take the first win around the Madring and another podium. The car was mega! I managed to have a really good start and then managed the tyres towards the end and also had the best lap of the race as well, so very happy."

THE CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Freddie Slater remains at the top of the Drivers' Championship on 141 points, but Ugo Ugochukwu takes a potentially vital two points out of his lead in P2, going onto 129. Théophile Nael's victory lifts him up to third ahead of Campos teammate Ernesto Rivera, 86 points to 81. Taito Kato remains fifth in the Standings on 73.

Campos Racing closes in on their second-consecutive Teams' title, extending their lead and going onto 296 points. TRIDENT is second on 213, with Van Amersfoort Racing taking third with 162. ART Grand Prix is now fourth on 157 points, with MP Motorsport fifth on 138.

UP NEXT

The FIA Formula 3 drivers are back in action later on Saturday with the first of two Feature Races this weekend. Taito Kato goes from Pole Position, while Ugo Ugochukwu will be aiming to take over the lead of the Drivers' Championship from P4 on the grid.

title: Deligny revels in ‘best qualifying of the year’ after strong performance in Madrid
excerpt:
Enzo Deligny qualified in the top six for both Madrid Feature Races after a strong qualifying performance

Enzo Deligny was delighted with the “best” and most “fun” qualifying of the season, with the Van Amersfoort Racing driver in strong position for all three races.

The French driver was fifth in Qualifying 1 and sixth in Qualifying 2, and after a tough run of results on Friday, he is delighted to finally show his potential.

“It’s the best quali of the year for me,” he said. “It was definitely my point to work on this year, so this is nice for the confidence, as it's for sure not an easy track.

“To be able to have two very solid qualifyings at the end of the year I think it's good for the morale and the confidence as well.

“It was the most fun quali of the year as well. I like the back-to-back qualis, obviously if it goes well in the first one.

Deligny was strong throughout both Qualifying sessions much to his delight

“But it's nice because you start with quite a heavy car, almost a full tank. You feel the fuel going down every lap and you're just fine-tuning every lap. So, honestly, it was really fun. The sunset as well made it quite cinematic, so it was cool.”

When asked what had changed to improve his qualifying form this weekend, Deligny believed that it was being in a positive place with the car that helped him feel more comfortable.
