title: Round 11 Post Qualifying 2 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following Qualifying Session 2 here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from Rodin Motorsport is Pedro Clerot. In second place, from Campos Racing, is Ugo Ugochukwu, and from MP Motorsport, capturing his second pole position of the season, is Tuukka Taponen. Congratulations, Tuukka. How does that one feel?

Tuukka Taponen: Yeah, it feels good. P3 in Q1 and P1 in the second qualifying. To be honest, I felt better with the driving in Q1, but luckily it was enough in Q2 to secure pole position. I am super happy to start on pole for Sunday's race.

FIA Formula 3: Can you take me through that pole-winning lap? How much commitment did it take from you?

Taponen: Yeah, I was one tenth off before starting the last push, and I was fifth or sixth. It was very tight there. We have been struggling the whole week in sector one, so it was just trying to minimise the time lost there and then do a good rest of the lap, which I did. It was a good lap at the end.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on that pole position. Ugo, coming to you next, congratulations. You have set yourself up well for a run at this championship. How good was the car for you today?

Ugo Ugochukwu: Yeah, for sure, it was a positive day for us. Two good qualifying sessions are exactly what we needed. I think we executed everything well, with no mistakes, and I got the lap in when we needed it. I am pretty happy overall and pretty happy with my lap. I think I maximised it to the limit. Some of the others were quite quick today, so P4 and P2, we will take it. I think we can look forward to the races and maximise our points.

FIA Formula 3: Moving on to the races, what is the mindset heading in? Is it the championship?

Ugochukwu: Yeah, for sure. I think two clean, or three clean races would be nice, picking up the points along the way. But we will see how the race unfolds. These are going to be the first races here in Madrid, so we do not fully know what to expect on the racing side. We will see if on Sunday we have an opportunity to go for the win. It would be nice to get another one under our belt. But overall, of course, points are the main thing. It is no secret that is what is going to get us the championship.

FIA Formula 3: And just your thoughts on the circuit. Do you have a favourite corner?

Ugochukwu: I would have to say Turns 10 and 11, before Monumental, the fast chicane. That is a super-tricky corner, and you can gain quite a bit of time when you are on the limit. We were quite quick through sector two, so maybe I am a little bit biased as well.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P2. Pedro, coming to you, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your final push run and what happened in the last corner?

Pedro Clerot: Yeah, I felt comfortable throughout the qualifying session, and I knew I had done a really good sector one by that time. I think that was our strong point, and I was chasing that feeling the whole day. I finally managed to do it on the last push of qualifying. I knew I was P2 at that time, less than a tenth behind Ugo, so I just committed for the whole lap. I was losing a bit of grip throughout the lap. On the previous lap, I think I was already quite sideways in the last sector. I just lost the rear of the car. Fortunately, by then it was the end of the session, so we did not really get affected. I think we would have been in the fight for pole with that lap, but I am just happy to be at the front again. We showed really good speed. We showed that we were up there in both qualifying sessions. It was a bit of a sad end, but I am happy that we could deliver when it mattered.

FIA Formula 3: Did you notice any track evolution through the session?

Clerot: For sure. We went, I think, almost a second quicker than Q1. Obviously, Q1 was a little bit messier. At least, I got fewer push laps in Q1. Q2 was a bit cleaner on my side and the driving felt a little bit better. But for sure, there was some track evolution since free practice today. We saw a big change in the times, so it was a bit different for us after two F1 sessions and two F2 sessions. It was the first time for us. I think we managed to do everything well today, and the results paid off.

title: Round 9 Post-Qualifying 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA FORMULA 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following Qualifying Session 1 here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from MP Motorsport is Tuukka Taponen. In second place, from Rodin Motorsport, is Pedro Clerot. And from ART Grand Prix, capturing his first pole position in Formula 3, is Taito Kato. Taito, congratulations. How does that one feel?

Taito Kato: It feels amazing. My first-ever pole position in Formula 3. It was an amazing weekend in Monza, and then back-to-back this weekend in Madrid. I think we have a good mindset, and the car was incredible during qualifying and really fun to drive here. In Madrid, you are really close to the wall. I was pushing on the edge, sometimes kissing the wall. That was really good. Finally, to get pole position, I am very happy with it.

FIA FORMULA 3: It is the first pole position for ART Grand Prix since Hungary 2024. How was the car today? You said it was good, but did it take a lot to get it into a window where you felt confident with it?

Kato: I think it was really good the whole year. There were just mistakes on my side, some traffic, or a bit of bad luck. Every time in Formula 3, it is really difficult to put everything together in one lap. Also, if you do not have any luck, it is really difficult to get pole position. So, finally, to get pole position in Formula 3, I am happy with the team and just want to say a massive thanks to the team. The car was incredible.

FIA FORMULA 3: The first-ever F3 qualifying here in Madrid. What did you make of the circuit?

Kato: Really good. Really, really fun to drive. The adrenaline was incredible in the car.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on the pole position. P2, Pedro Clerot, congratulations. Just 12-thousandths away from pole position. Can you take me through your session?

Pedro Clerot: Yeah, very close. I think it was an overall good session. It was a bit messy where I was. I only managed to do one push lap, and that was the one I had to make count. Together with the team, we saw that today was going to be all about putting a lap on the board, and I think we managed to do quite well. I felt really comfortable from free practice, and I knew the pace was there. Even though we were not so high up in free practice, I knew we were going to be okay. The car came alive in qualifying, and I was actually quite surprised to see I was P1 after the first run. I could not do my second lap because of traffic, and I could see on the TV that Kato was improving. I was thinking, please do not improve by too much. I could see it was just a small difference, but I am happy to be starting on the front row and happy for the team as well. We put a lot of work into this weekend, and it paid off.

FIA Formula 3: What did it feel like to drive the car on the limit in qualifying here?

Clerot: Very nice. Very, very nice. Overall, I am very happy for the team as well. Driving here is unique. You are close to every single wall. The more you risk, the higher the reward. Even though my lap was, I am not going to say on the safe side, but a very controlled lap, I was on the edge already. There was not a lot more in it, and for sure it feels really good to piece together a good lap around this place.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P2. P3, Tuukka Taponen. Tuukka, congratulations. How was that session for you?

Tuukka Taponen: Yeah, that was quite an alright session. I missed the first lap because I made a mistake, but after that it was quite clean for me. There was not any traffic, and all the laps I did were quite okay. I feel like my driving was better in this qualifying than in Q2, but it was quite okay, let us say.

FIA Formula 3: And just your thoughts on the circuit, on the track here. What did you think?

Taponen: It is a special track. You do not have any other tracks like that. You have many difficult corners, and like Taito said, it is very difficult to put everything together at this circuit. You just need to be good everywhere.

title: Alex Powell eyeing up Sprint Race possibilities after impressive Madrid Qualifying
excerpt:
Alex Powell put in one of the stand-out performances in Madrid Qualifying, finishing P10 in the first session to secure a second row start for the Sprint Race.

In what was just his second FIA Formula 3 Qualifying session, the PREMA Racing driver was on the pace from the outset, fighting for the top places.

Reflecting on the day, Powell said that he was very pleased with his and the team's performance, and that he felt a good result was a possibility from the opening laps of the weekend.

"A couple weeks ago I didn't even know I would be here," Powell said. "So very last minute, happy with the whole session to be honest. It was really strong for the whole team.

READ MORE

QUALIFYING: Kato takes pole in Q1 with Taponen on top in Q2; Ugochukwu seizes advantage in title fight

"We struggled a little bit this morning in Practice so I was a bit skeptical going into quali but the car was working really well, and I was happy with my driving.

"I think of course in retrospect I could have done a few things better but if I would have known I would have been a top 10 a couple weeks ago, I would have definitely taken it and signed the paper. So it's a good step for me, a good step forward but of course the aim is going to be to keep building from here."

After in-season testing last month, Practice offered the drivers one final look at the Madring circuit ahead of the Qualifying sessions.

With two grid-setting sessions this weekend, any mistake would have had a major impact, and Powell was pleased to have kept himself out of trouble whilst showing impressive pace.

The PREMA driver was P10 in Qualifying 1 around Madrid after an impressive performance

"It was very difficult in Practice to build things up. I felt really good though from the first push which was very nice, especially at a street circuit, you kind of have to have the rhythm from very early on.

"So I was really, really happy that I could feel a good rhythm from the very first push and then it was just about sustaining and building on that but we were pretty strong the whole time."

Though the PREMA driver was happy with his final Qualifying positions, he is targeting better things in the Sprint Race.

With a second row start and overtaking opportunities expected to be at a premium around the Spanish venue, Powell hopes to convert his starting position into a memorable result in just his second weekend.

"Looking back on it, I could have found a little bit here and a little bit there, but I'm sure everyone could say the same thing. Of course, as the session goes on, the intensity rises and you start to take a little bit more risk.

"I just missed a few tenths here and there to finish a little bit higher up but still it was a clean session for me, with no major scary moments let's say.

"The goal will be to move forward. We're on the second row of the grid for the Sprint, but the goal is still to move forward. The tyre management is still new to me, but I think I'm in a good position to make it work, so eyes forward."

title: QUALIFYING: Kato takes pole in Q1 with Taponen on top in Q2; Ugochukwu seizes advantage in title fight
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix driver Taito Kato claimed his maiden FIA Formula 3 Aramco Pole Position Award with a stunning performance in Qualifying 1, completing a 1:50.535 to beat Pedro Clerot by 0.012s.

In Qualifying 2, MP Motorsport driver Tuukka Taponen impressively beat title hopeful Ugo Ugochukwu to the Aramco Pole Position Award for Feature Race 2.

The Campos Racing driver was also fourth in Q1, while his rival Freddie Slater struggled, finishing 17th in the opening session, and eighth in Q2.

QUALIFYING 1

Kato was the first driver to cross the line and completed a 1:51.127. But no one else could match the ART driver with Alex Powell 0.161s behind in second.

It was not good news for TRIDENT, with Noah Stromsted’s sidepod coming loose after contact on the warmup lap with Kanato Le, while Slater complained of issues with the car.

On the second set of laps, Kato improved to a 1:50.639, with Jin Nakamura 0.218s behind in P2.

The Japanese drivers were demoted a position moments later when Rodin Motorsport’s Clerot went quickest on a 1:50.547.

In the battle for the title Slater was down in P11. The Championship leader was still complaining of issues with his car.

TRIDENT brought their driver in and fitted him with a new set of Hard tyres, while the rest of the field continued on.

Kato improved to a 1:50.535 to eclipse Clerot by 0.012s as Ugochukwu went to P4. Slater, despite the new rubber, came on the radio to complain of issues on his TRIDENT.

Elsewhere, Brando Badoer’s session looked to be over after he hit the barrier, with Rodin left in a race against time to fix his left rear suspension ahead of Qualifying 2.

Out on track, Kato could not improve on his final lap of Q1. But neither could his rivals, leaving him on pole for Feature Race 1, with Clerot settling for P2 ahead of Taponen.

Ugochukwu was fourth in front of Enzo Deligny, as Jin Nakamura followed in sixth ahead of Ernesto Rivera and Alessandro Giusti. Bruno del Pino ended up in P9, heading Alex Powell and Théophile Nael, while James Wharton rounded out the top 12.

The PREMA Racing driver is set to start Saturday’s Sprint Race from reverse grid pole, with Q1 setting the grid for the first race of the weekend.

In the title fight, Slater’s struggles continued, with a lockup at Turn 1 leaving him down in P17 in the first Qualifying session, much to his frustration.

QUALIFYING 2

After a short break the drivers were back out on track. This included Slater with TRIDENT having worked to fix his car in the break between the sessions.

The British driver looked to be back in the groove as he completed a 1:49.972 to go fastest, with Ugochukwu in second, over half a second behind his title rival.

Clerot and Badoer, who was back out on track with his car fixed, went up to second and third, although Nakamura split the Rodin duo moments later.

On the second set of laps, Kato jumped up to P1 only for Ugochukwu to demote him to P2 moments later with a 1:49.901.

Clerot continued his strong form to take over at the top with a 1:49.830. Slater, having set the fastest first sector, locked up on the entry to Turn 5, leaving him fifth.

Ugochukwu then reclaimed P1 with a 1:49.771 as Slater aborted his lap and returned to the pit lane. Clerot finished his next lap to go to P2, 0.069s off the Campos driver.

On the final lap of the day, Taponen went quickest on a 1:49.750. Ugochukwu came across the line but could not improve and stayed second.

Behind them, Clerot had been on for a fast lap, but he pushed too hard at the final corner, winding up in the barriers, bringing the session to an end.

This left Taponen on pole for Feature Race 2 ahead of Ugochukwu and Clerot, with Kato in fourth ahead of Mattia Colnaghi. Deligny was sixth ahead of Giusti and Slater, with Yevan David in P9. Rivera was 10th ahead of Badoer and Powell.

The first race of the Madrid weekend is on Saturday morning with lights out for the Sprint set for 11:05 local time.

title: PRACTICE: Nakamura fastest for Hitech in Madrid ahead of Kato
excerpt:
Jin Nakamura started the Madrid weekend fastest of all for Hitech. The Japanese driver recorded a 1:49.835 in the final minutes of the session to lead compatriot Taito Kato for ART Grand Prix by a tenth. Van Amersfoort Racing's Enzo Deligny completed the top three.

Kato was the first to set a time in the session, with the ART driver leading an early 1-2-3 for the French team on a 1:53.026.

The Japanese driver lowered his time to a 1:52.026 which was then bettered by Tuukka Taponen by just 0.037s.

Kato then returned to the top with 15 minutes to run on a 1:51.567 before title contender Ugo Ugochukwu went fastest with a 1:51.192.

The Campos Racing driver was flying on his next lap as he shaved off over half a second on his next attempt to lead the pack on a 1:50.587 with teammate Ernesto Rivera in P2.

Championship leader Freddie Slater replied with 20 minutes to go, lowering the benchmark effort to a 1:50.453.

Pedro Clerot had an earlier time good enough for P3 deleted, but he restored himself to the top three with just over 15 minutes to go with Taponen and then Rodin Motorsport teammate Brando Badoer in the top five.

Kato then went quickest once again, 0.060s ahead of Slater's time, before Fionn McLaughlin went just behind Clerot for Hitech in fifth.

Ugochukwu logged a 1:50.268 on his next lap to return to the top, before title rival Slater bettered that by just 0.072s.

Into the final five minutes and Enzo Deligny went to P2 just 0.069s off top spot before the next set of improvements arrived.

Kato lowered his best to a 1:49.936 to go P1, as Ugochukwu finished 0.064s down on that time in P2, 0.002s ahead of Rivera, with Slater fourth.

Nakamura then went quickest in the final minute, with Deligny moving himself back to third just as the Red Flag was thrown.

A crash for Nicola Lacorte in the final seconds brought Practice to a close, with the DAMS Lucas Oil driver OK after tagging the barriers at the exit of Turn 9.

Nakamura led Kato, Deligny, Ugochukwu and Rivera in the top five. Slater followed in sixth ahead of McLaughlin, Taponen, Clerot and Bruno Del Pino in the top 10.

There will be two Qualifying sessions this weekend, with the first getting underway at 18:25 local time. The second will follow immediately afterwards, with the green light scheduled for 18:55 local time.

title: PREVIEW: Round 9 in Madrid brings it all to a close
excerpt:
It is the final race weekend of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 season, and the paddock is heading to Madrid for what should to be an epic title showdown.

Freddie Slater and Ugo Ugochukwu look set to go head-to-head to be crowned Drivers’ Champion, while Campos Racing are on the brink of winning the Teams’ Title, but can TRIDENT stop them?

So as we get ready to hit the track in Madrid, here is everything you need to know…

WHAT TO EXPECT

Round 9 kicks off with Free Practice on Friday morning with the green light set for 09:55 local time.

There will be a slight twist to the weekend format in Madrid, as we will have two Feature Races, which means we have two Qualifying sessions.

The first of which is set to start at 18:25 local time. After those first 20 minutes of action, the drivers will hit the track for the second Qualifying session at 18:55 local time.

The top 12 from Qualifying 1 will be reversed for Saturday morning’s Sprint Race at 11:05 local time. That session will also set the grid for the first Feature Race at 18:00 later that day.

Qualifying 2 will set the order for second and final Feature Race of the weekend, with lights out scheduled for 09:45 local time on Sunday morning.

Niccolò Maccagnani is set to replace Christian Ho at Rodin Motorsport for the final round of the season.

AIX Racing have confirmed that Car 26 has been withdrawn from the event as Ricardo Escotto cannot take part under medical grounds.

DAMS Lucas Oil have also withdrawn Car 31 from the race weekend.

STAT PACK

The Madring is made up of 22 corners and is 5.414km long.

The drivers got their first taste of the circuit at a two-day test last month where Campos Racing’s Ugo Ugochukwu set the fastest time of a 1:49.034.

Ugochukwu led both morning sessions during last month’s test, while Slater topped the timesheets in the afternoon runs.

Slater and Ugochukwu head into the finale separated by 15 points, with Ernesto Rivera and Théophile Nael still retaining an outside chance of claiming the title.

With Nicola Lacorte’s victory at Monza, 13 different drivers have now won a race in 2026 — a new record for the most winners in a single Formula 3 season.

FROM THE GRID – Bruno del Pino, Van Amersfoort Racing

“It’s very fast, really fast. But it’s also tight, it feels like Jeddah in a way. But it’s a home race so that’s exciting.

“There are not many places to overtake, because the run to T1 is not a very long, but there's a very long straight afterwards. So maybe there.

“I’d say the most difficult part will be making use of the high-speed sections and getting close to the walls, but everything else will be quite quick and easy to adapt.

“It's my home race. I have two home race weekends. So, Barcelona, because I was born there, and Madrid because I'm half from Madrid, and I live in Madrid. It is exciting.”

TECHNICAL PREVIEW

Pierre-Alain Michot, FIA Formula 3 Technical Director

“While it is a new track on the calendar the Madring is known to the drivers and the teams as they had two days of in-season testing here last month.

“It is a high-speed street track with many changes of directions, which means the teams will put a huge emphasis on downforce, making sure their cars are aerodynamically balanced in both Qualifying and the races.

“Tyres will also be a point of focus, with temperatures expected to be high, and with nature of the layout, those who take care of their Pirelli rubber will benefit the most.”

PIRELLI PREVIEW

The Hard compound has been selected for the Formula 3 weekend at Madring. Drivers have already had a first taste of the new circuit in the Spanish capital during the two-day test held at the end of August. Tyre degradation is expected to remain limited and, should temperatures be relatively low, aided by the circuit's altitude, graining could become a factor. Qualifying could prove to be one of the most decisive and demanding sessions of the weekend, given the limited overtaking opportunities offered by the circuit. Furthermore, as this is a new track on which drivers still have limited experience, the likelihood of safety car interventions and red flags remains high.
